Class PublicSanitationWaterGridEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier2.theories.PublicSanitationWaterGridEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class PublicSanitationWaterGridEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine

Public Sanitation & Municipal Clean Water Grid Engine

Models the biophysical and epidemiological mechanisms underlying the Preston Curve (1975) and Omran's Epidemiological Transition (1971).

Scientific Foundations

  • David Cutler & Grant Miller (2005) The Role of Public Health Improvements in Health Advances: The Twentieth-Century United States, Demography 42(1): 1–22.
  • Abdel R. Omran (1971) The Epidemiological Transition: A Theory of the Epidemiology of Population Change, Milbank Mem. Fund Q. 49(4): 509–538.
  • Samuel H. Preston (1975) The Changing Relation between Mortality and Level of Economic Development, Population Studies 29(2): 231–248.

Mechanistic Dynamics

In dense human agglomerations ($N \ge 2\,000$ hab), unchanneled wastewater and shallow contaminated wells create an endogenous waterborne pathogen load (cholera, dysentery, typhoid) scaling with urban fecal density: $$\lambda_{\text{fecal}} = \frac{N_{\text{cell}}}{A_{\text{cell}} \cdot (1 + \text{AquiferFlush})}$$ Clean water aqueducts, subterranean masonry sewage grids, sand filtration, and municipal chlorination reduce pathogen transmission directly as a function of dedicated physical sanitary infrastructure ($K_{\text{sanitation}}$), without any arbitrary calendar-year date check.
